Definition: from G3534 and G2992; victorious over the people; Nicolaüs, a heretic:--Nicolaus.
BiblicalUsage: Nicolas is a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven the multitude chooses to serve, named beside Stephen and Philip. The book of Acts shows him chosen for good report, and later tradition ties his name to the Nicolaitans — but in Acts itself he stands among the seven.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Nicolas should be read as Acts reads him: a man the whole church chose, whose name later writers argued over, but whose place is among the seven.
